question: Does serving the learned pre-ranker make a bot win more games than the ordering it replaces, at a real clock?
why_it_is_separate_from_the_metrics: Recall and NDCG say the ranker agrees with the teacher more often. Strength is a different claim and the corpus cannot support it: the metrics hold the search constant and ignore the clock, while the pre-rank pass is paid out of the turn budget before the deadline is consulted. A ranker that orders better and costs more can lose. Only a game decides, which is why this protocol exists and why nothing in results-v1.md is allowed to stand in for it.

prerequisite.name: engine-bump
prerequisite.compares: dicechess-bot-gcp-onnx on engine 0.12.0 against the same bot on 0.12.2, every other setting identical
prerequisite.why: The pre-ranker seam (`PreRankModel`) first exists in engine v0.12.1, so the bot must move off 0.12.0 before the real arm can run at all. That bump is not neutral: v0.12.0..v0.12.2 includes `fix: preserve en passant through occupied target`, a rules change, alongside graph validation at session construction. Moving a production bot's engine is exactly the class of change this organisation asks for arena evidence on — the same point that went unmeasured when Dependabot moved hunter from 0.9.1 to 0.12.0.
prerequisite.stop_on: If the bump costs measurable strength, the pre-ranker arm is blocked on understanding why rather than on scheduling.

primary.name: prerank-slot
primary.compares: the same bot image and engine, twice, differing only in what fills the pre-rank slot
primary.control: `material` — the engine's default `ExpectimaxSearch.materialBatch`, which is what dicechess-bot-gcp-onnx and -4 run today
primary.also_worth_running: `PRE_RANK_WITH_MODEL=true`, the leaf model reused as a pre-ranker, which is what dexus-atlas-1 runs. It is the incumbent for that bot and the corpus says it orders worse than material at three of four widths, so its arena result is interesting whichever way it falls.

treatment_identity.why_pinned_here: Without it 'the learned pre-ranker' names a class rather than a thing, and a later run could put a different, equally valid move-prerank package behind the same label and be compared against this one. The manifest already binds the graph by digest; this protocol binds which manifest.
treatment_identity.rule: A run whose loaded package does not report this digest is a run of a different treatment and must be reported under its own identity, not merged with this one.

held_constant: the bot image, so the two sides differ by configuration and not by build
the pre-rank package itself, by the modelSha256 recorded under arms.primary.treatment_identity
the leaf model and the rescore model, with their digests recorded
`ORACLE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT`, because width is a lever of its own and a width verdict measured while something else moved is not a verdict
the opening book, the transposition table settings, the time policy and the overhead buffer
the arena's dice seeds, which the engine owns; mirrored colour pairs mean both sides face the same rolls

clock.why: Fixed time, and the harshest control for a treatment that spends time. The pre-rank pass costs about 1.5 microseconds per candidate and 30 ms on the widest root measured, so at a long control its cost disappears and only ordering quality is tested. If the learned ranker wins at 1+0 it wins where the cost is hardest to hide.
clock.confirmation_rule: Run only if 1+0 is positive, and report both. A verdict at one control is a verdict at that control — hunter's own scaladoc records a width comparison whose sign flipped between an untimed and a clocked run.

sampling.pairing: mirrored colour pairs, so each opening position is played from both sides
sampling.stopping_rule: SPRT with bounds 0 and 20 Elo at alpha = beta = 0.05
sampling.cap_rationale: The stopping rule usually ends earlier; the cap bounds the machine time when it does not. An SPRT that stops at its H1 boundary biases the point estimate away from zero, so the recorded effect size is an upper bound and the protocol says so wherever it is quoted.
sampling.report: games, win/draw/loss, the log-likelihood ratio, the 95% interval, and the flag losses on each side

outcome_at_cap.primary_arm: Inconclusive, and inconclusive is not adoption. The cap result stands as the result: 'no effect of the preregistered size detectable at this sample', with the observed difference and its interval reported as a bound rather than as a finding.
outcome_at_cap.confirmation: Not run. The confirmation rule is 'only if 1+0 is positive', and inconclusive is not positive.
outcome_at_cap.reruns: More games against the same configuration require a new protocol version naming the larger cap in advance. Extending a run after seeing where it stopped is optional stopping, and it is the way an inconclusive result becomes a positive one without any new evidence.
outcome_at_cap.prerequisite_arm: Different, because its null is the thing being hoped for. Reaching the cap without a boundary means no strength difference of the preregistered size was detected between the two engines, which is bounded evidence rather than none — record the bound and proceed. That is more than the bump would otherwise have had.

invalidates_the_run: any flag loss attributable to the harness rather than the bot, because a bot that never answered did not play
a difference in the recorded model digests between the two sides
the two sides resolving different engine versions
a container restart mid-run, which resets the transposition table and is not a property of either configuration

decision_rule.adopt: SPRT accepts H1 at 1+0 and the 3+2 confirmation does not contradict it
decision_rule.reject: SPRT accepts H0, or the confirmation control reverses the sign
decision_rule.note: A pre-ranker that measures better on recall and NDCG and does not win games is not adopted. That is the entire reason this arm exists, and the metrics are not permitted to overrule it.
decision_rule.inconclusive: SPRT reaches the cap without a boundary. Not adopted, and recorded as a bound on the effect rather than as evidence of no effect. The likely reading is the one the metrics already reached: at this sample the corpus and the arena both run out of resolution before the question does.

harness.existing: dicechess-hunter/referee/run.sh — the engine's own arena, which owns the dice RNG, the seeds, the clocks and the rules; the script stands two containers up and points the arena at them. It already runs a hunter container against an ONNX container over the webhook protocol, with SPRT and clock presets.
harness.change_needed: The compose file pairs hunter with one ONNX service. This arena needs the same ONNX image twice with different environments, which is a compose change rather than a new harness.
harness.do_not: Write a second arena. Nothing here should reimplement a game loop; the engine owns the rules and the dice.

blocked_on.capability: dicechess-bot-gcp-onnx cannot be told to use a dedicated pre-ranker. `PRE_RANK_WITH_MODEL` is a boolean that reuses the leaf model, and the bot pins engine 0.12.0, which predates `PreRankModel`.
blocked_on.required_change: Move the bot to engine >= 0.12.1 and add configuration for a pre-rank package directory, wired through `PreRankModel.fromPackage`, defaulting to off.
blocked_on.already_verified: The artifact itself is ready: `ModelPackage.load` accepts the exported `model.onnx` + `manifest.json` with role `move-prerank` and 9 features, `PreRankModel.fromPackage` accepts the package, and the same loader refuses it when asked for `position-value`. So the seam and the artifact agree; only the host does not know how to ask.

not_covered: hunter, whose first phase is `HunterEval.cheapScore` and which does not use this seam
any claim about strength at controls other than the two above
whether a different candidate limit would suit the learned ranker better — width is a separate lever and mixing it in would confound this
